edges.description: Bacilli and their antigens in the pericardium elicit the early fibrinous inflammatory exudate.
The early granulomatous inflammation recruits antigen-specific T cells into the pericardium.
Fibrinous pericardial inflammation produces pericarditic chest pain.
Fibrin-coated inflamed pericardial layers produce a friction rub.
The lymphocytic inflammatory response drives accumulation of a protein-rich exudate in the pericardial sac.
The T-cell and macrophage response releases the cytokines that make up the profibrotic pericardial milieu.
The systemic inflammatory response to tuberculous infection produces fever.
Night sweats are a constitutional symptom of the tuberculous inflammatory response.
Weight loss is a constitutional consequence of chronic tuberculous inflammation.
The accumulating exudate is the pericardial effusion seen on imaging.
A large or rapidly accumulating effusion raises intrapericardial pressure and compresses the cardiac chambers.
Haemodynamically significant compression is cardiac tamponade.
Impaired filling and contraction produce the heart failure syndrome.
Reduced cardiac output under compression lowers blood pressure.
Compensatory tachycardia accompanies reduced stroke volume.
Ventricular interdependence under tamponade exaggerates the inspiratory fall in systolic pressure.
Reduced cardiac output and venous congestion cause breathlessness.
The profibrotic milieu is proposed to drive organisation of the exudate into fibrous pericardium; the intervening cellular steps are not established in human tissue.
The fibrosing pericardium contracts on the cardiac chambers.
Impaired diastolic filling by fibrotic pericardium is constrictive pericarditis.
Raised systemic venous pressure behind the constricted right heart produces ascites.
Raised systemic venous pressure produces peripheral oedema.
Constriction is the second mechanism of the heart failure syndrome.
Granulomatous infiltration of the myocardium is a tuberculous myocarditis.
Myocardial infiltration disturbs electrical conduction and produces ventricular arrhythmia.
Arrhythmogenic myocardial infiltration causes sudden cardiac death, whose risk is not removed by antituberculous therapy.
Myocardial infiltration can impair contractile function and produce heart failure.
In HIV co-infection, spread to the pericardium is most often by hematogenous dissemination as part of disseminated tuberculosis.

nodes.description: Six weeks of adjunctive prednisolone in the IMPI trial did not reduce the composite of death, tamponade or constriction, but reduced constriction and hospitalisation, at the cost of more HIV-associated cancer.
